newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Stena Line still confident of P&O JV nod.
newsitem.headline: Stena Line still confident of P&O JV nod.

text.p: Swedish ferry operator Stena Line AB said on Monday it still expected the European Union (EU) commission to approve its proposed merger of cross-channel ferry operations with Britain's P&O.
The plan involves the two ferry lines pooling resources on Dover-Calais, Dover-Zeebrugge, and Newhaven-Dieppe routes to compete mainly with the Anglo-French Tunnel operator Eurotunnel Plc.
"There is nothing to indicate anything other than things are going OK," Stena Line spokesman Goran Ekstedt told Reuters.
Stena Line and P&O, the Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Company, received a 'letter of serious doubts' from the EU commission in early June regarding the merger.
The company said it was now expecting approval via a so-called 'letter of comfort'.
The UK Monopolies and Mergers Commission completed a study of the merger in May and has passed on its recommendations to the Department of Trade and Industry.
The cooperation also requires approval from the British government. The French government has already given its approval.
Ekstedt said Stena Line has had no indications when a decision from either the EU or the British government could be expected.
But he said the companies did not expect the approvals to take effect before the high season at the start of August.
"It seems that we will miss the high season this year," Ekstedt said.
Ekstedt declined to comment on what impact restructuring costs for the new company, to be called P&O Stena Line, would have in 1997.
The new company has estimated total restructuring costs would be 35 million pounds sterling ($58 million).
"The largest part will certainly hit this year if the decision comes within the next few days and no conditions are put on it," Ekstedt said.
He said it was too early to speculate about possible savings.
Stena Line had earlier estimated that the new company expected cost savings of about 75 million sterling from the company's fixed costs of around 280 million sterling.
The new group's operations will be controlled jointly and equally by the British and Swedish operators, but Stena Line will own 40 percent and P&O will hold a 60 percent financial stake.
